name: La Mazmorra de la Roca Oscura

sentences.base_language: The three brothers stand at the entrance of the dungeon.
sentences.target_language: Los tres hermanos están en la entrada de la mazmorra.
sentences.grammarNote:
**están** uses **estar** for location — the brothers are physically at the entrance, a temporary position in space.
**de la mazmorra** = of the dungeon — **de + la** does not contract (only **de + el → del**).

sentences.base_language: It is dark, cold, and smells like old stone.
sentences.target_language: Está oscura, fría y huele a piedra vieja.
sentences.grammarNote:
**Está oscura, fría** — **estar** for the current conditions inside the dungeon (temporary states of darkness and coldness).
**huele a** = smells like — **oler** is an o→ue stem-changing verb, and takes the preposition **a** to mean 'smells of/like': **huele a café**, **huele a peligro** (smells like danger).

sentences.base_language: Jeffrey's ranger character moves slowly to the front.
sentences.target_language: El personaje explorador de Jeffrey avanza lentamente hasta el frente.
sentences.grammarNote:
**avanza** = advances/moves forward (él/ella present of **avanzar**, regular -ar). Preterite yo spelling change: **avancé** (z→c).
**hasta el frente** = to the front — **hasta** marks the destination or limit point of movement.

sentences.base_language: Suddenly, three goblins jump out from behind the rocks!
sentences.target_language: ¡De repente, tres duendes saltan desde detrás de las rocas!
sentences.grammarNote:
**De repente** = suddenly — a very common narrative time marker; also **de pronto**.
**desde detrás de** = from behind — Spanish stacks prepositions naturally: **desde** (from) + **detrás de** (behind) + **las rocas** (the rocks).

sentences.base_language: Jeffrey shouts: 'Fighters to the front! Wizard, cast a spell!'
sentences.target_language: Jeffrey grita: —¡Guerreros, al frente! ¡Mago, lanza un hechizo!
sentences.grammarNote:
**¡al frente!** = to the front! — **al** = contraction of **a + el** (mandatory in Spanish).
**¡Lanza!** is the tú affirmative imperative of **lanzar** (to cast/throw) — drop the -s from the tú present: **lanzas → lanza**.

sentences.base_language: One brother attacks a goblin with his sword.
sentences.target_language: Un hermano ataca a un duende con su espada.
sentences.grammarNote:
**ataca a** — the personal **a** is required before the goblin as a direct object here, even though goblins are fictional beings (treated as animate entities in gaming).
**con su espada** = with his sword — **su** agrees with **espada** in use but is determined by context (it means 'his' here).

sentences.base_language: He rolls a natural twenty and scores a critical hit!
sentences.target_language: ¡Saca un veinte natural y logra un golpe crítico!
sentences.grammarNote:
**saca** (he gets/rolls) — **sacar** (to take out/get) is used colloquially for rolling dice and getting a score: **sacar un diez** (to roll a ten).
**logra** = achieves/scores (él/ella present of **lograr**, regular -ar).

sentences.base_language: The goblin falls to the ground.
sentences.grammarNote:
**cae** = falls (él/ella present of **caer**, to fall) — irregular yo form: **caigo**. Full present: caigo, caes, cae, caemos, caéis, caen.
**al suelo** = to the ground — **al** = **a + el** (mandatory contraction).

sentences.base_language: The other brother uses a potion to heal himself.
sentences.target_language: El otro hermano usa una poción para curarse.
sentences.grammarNote:
**curarse** = to heal oneself — reflexive verb **curar** + reflexive pronoun **se** attached to infinitive.
**para + infinitive** = in order to / so that — **para curarse** = in order to heal himself.

sentences.base_language: Jeffrey's ranger fires two arrows at the last goblin.
sentences.target_language: El explorador de Jeffrey dispara dos flechas al último duende.
sentences.grammarNote:
**dispara** = fires/shoots (él/ella present of **disparar**, regular -ar).
**al último duende** — **al** = **a + el**; **último** (last/final) is an adjective that precedes the noun here for emphasis, agreeing masculine with **duende**.

sentences.target_language: Las dos flechas dan en el blanco.
sentences.grammarNote:
**dan en el blanco** = hit the mark/target — **dar en el blanco** is a fixed expression meaning 'to hit the target' (literally 'to give on the white [bullseye]').
**dan** = they give (third-person plural of **dar**, irregular: doy, das, da, damos, dais, dan).

sentences.base_language: The goblins are defeated. The party continues deeper into the dungeon.
sentences.target_language: Los duendes están derrotados. El grupo continúa más adentro de la mazmorra.
sentences.grammarNote:
**están derrotados** — **estar** + past participle for a resulting state: the goblins are in the state of having been defeated.
**más adentro de** = deeper into — **adentro** (inside/deep) + **más** (more) creates a comparison of depth.

sentences.base_language: At the end of a long corridor, they find a locked chest.
sentences.target_language: Al final de un largo corredor, encuentran un cofre cerrado con llave.
sentences.grammarNote:
**Al final de** = at the end of — **al** = **a + el**; a very useful phrase for storytelling.
**cerrado con llave** = locked — literally 'closed with key'; this is the standard Spanish expression for something being locked.

sentences.base_language: Inside the chest there is gold, gems, and an enchanted sword.
sentences.target_language: Dentro del cofre hay oro, gemas y una espada encantada.
sentences.grammarNote:
**Hay** = there is/there are — invariable regardless of singular or plural. Here it introduces three items in a list.
**encantada** agrees feminine with **espada** — past participle **encantar** used as adjective: encantado/encantada/encantados/encantadas.

sentences.base_language: 'This is not the village's main treasure,' Jeffrey says. 'The dragon still has it.'
sentences.target_language: —Este no es el tesoro principal del pueblo —dice Jeffrey—. El dragón todavía lo tiene.
sentences.grammarNote:
**todavía** = still/yet — equivalent to **aún** (with accent). **Todavía no** = not yet.
**lo tiene** = he has it — **lo** is the masculine singular direct object pronoun replacing **el tesoro**: placed before the conjugated verb **tiene**.

sentences.base_language: They collect the loot and prepare for the final battle.
sentences.target_language: Recogen el botín y se preparan para la batalla final.
sentences.grammarNote:
**recogen** = they collect (third-person plural of **recoger**, to collect/pick up) — irregular yo form: **recojo** (g→j before o/a).
**se preparan** = they prepare themselves — reflexive verb **prepararse**: the reflexive pronoun **se** agrees with the third-person plural subject.
